concepts.name: de Broglie wavelength
concepts.statement: At low temperature the atoms are best described as matter wavepackets, whose size is set by the de Broglie wavelength.

concepts.name: Condensation criterion
concepts.statement: The transition between primarily classical and primarily quantum mechanical behaviour occurs when the atomic wavepackets overlap, at a density and temperature where the phase space density reaches ζ(3/2) ≈ 2.612.

concepts.name: Atomic density
concepts.statement: The density n of a gas counts its atoms per unit volume.

concepts.name: Critical temperature
concepts.statement: Below the critical temperature T_c set by the gas's density, a macroscopic number of Bose atoms occupy the lowest energy state, even at finite temperature.

concepts.name: Bose condensation
concepts.statement: Bose condensation, a macroscopic occupation of the lowest energy state, occurs only if the atom cloud is both dense and cold, so that its phase space density is large.

concepts.name: Indistinguishability and statistical weight
concepts.statement: The weight of an arrangement is the number of ways it can be formed; for ten particles in two states the {5, 5} arrangement outweighs {10, 0} by 252 when they are distinguishable, while for indistinguishable particles the two have equal weight.

concepts.name: Bose-Einstein distribution
concepts.statement: In the grand canonical ensemble N Bose particles with total energy E distribute themselves among the energy levels ϵ_i in the most random way, the Bose-Einstein distribution.

concepts.name: Chemical potential
concepts.statement: The chemical potential μ fixes the number of particles in the grand canonical ensemble; a gas and a surface in equilibrium have equal chemical potentials.

concepts.name: Keeping the ground state out of the integral
concepts.statement: When the sums are converted into integrals over the density of states g(ϵ), the atoms in the ground state ϵ₀ must be kept as a separate term.

concepts.name: Condensate fraction of an ideal gas
concepts.statement: For non-interacting, unconfined bosons the ground state holds N(1 − (T/T_c)^{3/2}) atoms below T_c; in a three-dimensional harmonic trap the power is 3.

concepts.name: Superfluid helium as a depleted condensate
concepts.statement: Superfluid helium is a strongly correlated fluid in which only about 10% of the atoms are in the ground state: a Bose condensate with a strong quantum depletion imposed by the interactions.

concepts.name: Condensation as a metastable state
concepts.statement: In thermodynamic equilibrium every material becomes solid or liquid before it is cold and dense enough to Bose condense, so a gaseous condensate must be a metastable state that lasts long enough to measure.

concepts.name: Spin-polarized hydrogen
concepts.statement: Spin-polarized hydrogen cannot recombine into H₂ and stays polarized for days; it was cryogenically cooled on superfluid helium walls and magnetically trapped, until spin-flip collisions on the walls stopped it at low temperature.

concepts.name: Stability window of the alkalis
concepts.statement: At very low densities and nano-Kelvin temperatures recombination needs a three-particle collision, whose rate is small beside the two-body elastic scattering rate, so the alkali gases can be evaporatively cooled to condensation.

concepts.name: Trapping and cooling
concepts.statement: Atoms must be cold to be trapped, and once trapped they can be cooled further because the trap breaks their thermal contact with the outside.

concepts.name: Atoms sticking to surfaces
concepts.statement: The potential above a surface supports many bound states into which an atom quickly relaxes, so above about 1 mK an atom that touches a solid sticks with probability essentially one.

concepts.name: Surface resonance time
concepts.statement: Equating the flux onto the surface with the rate of leaving gives the time an atom stays stuck, exponentially sensitive to its binding energy.

concepts.name: Trap depth
concepts.statement: The depth of a trap is expressed as the highest temperature of the atoms it can confine.

concepts.name: Buffer gas cooling
concepts.statement: A cold buffer gas cools any atom or molecule to its own temperature, near 1 K, before it reaches the chamber walls; the gas is then pumped away and the atoms held magnetically.

concepts.name: Magnetic trapping
concepts.statement: Magnetic traps confine atoms with nonzero angular momentum through the energy g_Fμ_Bm_FB_z; since Maxwell's equations forbid static field maxima, only weak-field-seeking states can be trapped.

concepts.name: Adiabatic following and Majorana flips
concepts.statement: An atom stays trapped if the field direction turns slowly beside the Larmor frequency; too fast a turn causes spin flips that eject it.

concepts.name: Quadrupole trap and its hole
concepts.statement: Anti-Helmholtz coils make a field linear in each direction with a zero at the centre, where adiabatic following fails, so the trap acts as if it had a hole; the time-orbiting potential (TOP) trap plugs it by moving the zero.

concepts.name: Ioffe-Pritchard trap
concepts.statement: A two-dimensional quadrupole combined with Helmholtz coils gives a nearly harmonic trap with a nonzero field minimum.

concepts.name: Evaporative cooling
concepts.statement: The atoms that boil off the top of the trap carry more than the average energy, so the remaining atoms re-thermalize to a lower temperature; lowering the barrier keeps the cooling rate up.

concepts.name: RF knife
concepts.statement: RF coupling to an untrapped hyperfine state, resonant where the trap's Zeeman shift matches it, cuts the hottest atoms from the edges of the trap; sweeping the frequency moves the knife toward the centre, a Landau-Zener crossing that limits the trap depth.

concepts.name: Competing loss processes
concepts.statement: Three-body recombination, inelastic (dipolar) collisions that flip the spin and background-gas collisions limit the lifetime of trapped atoms, so evaporation must be fast enough to finish but slow enough to let the atoms rethermalize.

concepts.name: Atoms in a linear trap
concepts.statement: In a spherical linear trap the thermal density falls as e^{−ηρ/ρ₀}, with η = μB₀/k_BT, so the trap holds 6V₀n₀/η³ atoms: η³ is a compression factor over the geometric volume.

concepts.name: Two-body inelastic loss
concepts.statement: Two-body losses go as the square of the density, so the dipolar loss from the trap carries a factor 1/8 beside the atom number.

concepts.name: Evaporation rate
concepts.statement: Atoms evaporate as fast as elastic collisions, with cross-section σ_el, refill the pool of hot atoms.

concepts.name: Good and bad collisions
concepts.statement: Atoms lost to dipolar relaxation heat the sample, so evaporation succeeds only if the evaporative loss beats the inelastic loss, which needs a favourable ratio of elastic to inelastic rates, g_in ≪ g_el, as in the alkalis.

concepts.name: Absorption imaging
concepts.statement: Imaging the shadow of the cloud in a resonant beam measures its transmission e^{−d/2}, set by the optical depth.

concepts.name: Time-of-flight imaging
concepts.statement: Released from the trap, the cloud expands and maps its initial momentum distribution onto position, which is then imaged; its shape tells the parabolic condensate from the gaussian thermal cloud.

concepts.name: Phase-contrast imaging
concepts.statement: Off resonance, the cloud imprints a phase φ = −δd/2 on the beam that interference with a reference reads out, exciting so few atoms that one condensate can be imaged many times.

concepts.name: Dilute quantum gas
concepts.statement: In a dilute gas the interatomic spacing is large beside the range r₀ of the van der Waals tail, and below the degeneracy temperature n^{−1/3}r₀ ≪ 1 implies kr₀ ≪ 1, the small parameter of the scattering theory.

concepts.name: van der Waals potential
concepts.statement: Between well-separated neutral ground-state atoms the dipole-dipole interaction in second order gives an attractive potential falling as 1/r⁶.

concepts.name: Collision as scattering off a fixed potential
concepts.statement: When the centre of mass decouples, a collision of two atoms is a single body of reduced mass μ = m₁m₂/(m₁ + m₂) scattering off the fixed potential U(r).

concepts.name: Scattering amplitude
concepts.statement: Far from the scatterer the wavefunction is the incident plane wave plus an outgoing spherical wave weighted by the scattering amplitude f_k(θ).

concepts.name: Scattering cross-section
concepts.statement: The partial cross-section is the scattering rate into a solid angle over the incident intensity, |f_k(θ)|² for elastic collisions, and its integral over all angles is the total cross-section, an area.

concepts.name: Born approximation
concepts.statement: Expanding in the potential, the scattering amplitude is the Fourier transform of the potential; at low energy only the first term survives, so the scattered wave is isotropic.

concepts.name: Partial wave expansion
concepts.statement: For a spherical potential the wavefunction expands in Legendre polynomials into uncoupled radial equations, solved separately inside and outside r₀ and matched where r₀ < r < 1/k.

concepts.name: Scattering phase shift
concepts.statement: Each partial wave leaves the potential with a phase shift δ_l fixed by the matched coefficients, which vanishes as k → 0, and the scattering amplitude is a sum over them.

concepts.name: s-wave dominance
concepts.statement: In the ultracold limit kr₀ ≪ 1 the partial amplitude f_l ≈ cr₀(r₀k)^{2l}, so all but the s-wave amplitude f₀ may be neglected unless a resonance intervenes.

concepts.name: s-wave scattering length
concepts.statement: The s-wave radial wavefunction outside the potential goes as 1 − a/r; the scattering length a is the intercept of its asymptote and alone characterizes s-wave scattering.

concepts.name: Signs of the scattering length
concepts.statement: A hard sphere has a = r₀, a finite repulsive potential 0 < a < r₀, and a shallow attractive well with no bound state a negative a; each new bound state changes its sign.

concepts.name: s-wave pseudopotential
concepts.statement: In the ultracold limit every potential with scattering length a acts like a delta-function pseudopotential, whose first-order shift is the mean-field energy and gives the chemical potential.

concepts.name: Scattering of identical particles
concepts.statement: For identical particles the two scattering angles add with ε = ±1, so identical bosons see their s-wave cross-section doubled and identical fermions do not interact in the s-wave channel.

concepts.name: Matter wave through a cloud of atoms
concepts.statement: A matter wave crossing a dilute slab of scatterers picks up a phase as light does in a medium, corresponding to the mean-field energy 4πℏ²an/m.

concepts.name: Cold, dilute and strongly interacting
concepts.statement: Where the scattering length far exceeds r₀, ka ∼ 1 while kr₀ ≪ 1: a gas that is cold and dilute yet strongly interacting, purely through the s-wave channel.

concepts.name: Weakly bound state
concepts.statement: For large positive a the resonance is tied to a weakly bound state of the van der Waals tail with energy −ℏ²/2μa², into which molecules can be formed.

concepts.name: Feshbach resonance
concepts.statement: When a bound state of a closed channel nears the threshold of the open channel, a small coupling between them makes the scattering length diverge; tuning a magnetic field moves the resonance and so controls the interactions.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian of a dilute Bose gas
concepts.statement: A weakly interacting dilute gas is described by single-particle terms and two-body interactions, the latter replaced by the s-wave pseudopotential of strength U₀ = 4πℏ²a/m.

concepts.name: Second quantization of matter
concepts.statement: Creation and annihilation operators add or remove an atom from single-atom states; their commutation (bosons) or anticommutation (fermions) builds the symmetry of the many-body wavefunction in.

concepts.name: Matter field operator
concepts.statement: The Fourier transform of the momentum-mode operators is the field operator ψ̂(r), which annihilates a particle at position r.

concepts.name: Second-quantized Hamiltonian
concepts.statement: With the s-wave pseudopotential the gas's Hamiltonian is a single integral over the field operator.

concepts.name: Non-interacting condensate at T = 0
concepts.statement: Without interactions every atom piles into the single-particle ground state, the Gaussian of the harmonic trap with oscillator lengths a_j² = ℏ/mω_j.

concepts.name: Gross-Pitaevskii equation
concepts.statement: When the field operator is close to a classical coherent field and its fluctuations are small, the condensate obeys a Schrödinger equation with a nonlinear term, its wavefunction ψ normalized to the atom number.

concepts.name: Symmetry-breaking description
concepts.statement: Replacing ψ̂ by the c-number ψ assumes the atom field is a coherent state with an arbitrary phase and an uncertain atom number, valid for large atom numbers.

concepts.name: Ground state of a condensate
concepts.statement: Atom number is conserved, so the ground state is a stationary solution of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation evolving at the chemical potential; the ratio of mean-field to trap energy, ∼ Na/a_t, sets its character.

concepts.name: Trap length and frequency
concepts.statement: A harmonic trap of frequency ω_t has a characteristic size a_t, the oscillator length of its ground state.

concepts.name: Thomas-Fermi approximation
concepts.statement: For strong repulsive interactions the kinetic energy is neglected and the density is (μ − V)/U₀ where V < μ; in a harmonic trap the chemical potential and the size grow with Na/a_t.

concepts.name: Healing length
concepts.statement: Near a wall the condensate falls off smoothly over the healing length ξ, where the kinetic energy of the variation matches the interaction energy; in a dilute gas it spans many atoms.

concepts.name: Condensate density
concepts.statement: |ψ(r)|² is the condensate's spatial density, n₀ in a uniform condensate.

concepts.name: Bogoliubov approximation
concepts.statement: Linearizing the Heisenberg equation in small fluctuations δψ̂ about the mean field and expanding them in bosonic normal modes gives the Bogoliubov equations for the condensate's excitations.

forms.latex: \delta\hat{\psi} = e^{-i\mu t/\hbar}\sum_j\left(u_j\hat{\alpha}_j e^{-i\omega_j t} - v_j^*\hat{\alpha}_j^\dagger e^{i\omega_j t}\right)

concepts.name: Bogoliubov spectrum
concepts.statement: In a uniform condensate the excitations obey ℏω_q = √(ϵ_q² + 2n₀U₀ϵ_q): sound-like at small q and particle-like at large q, crossing over near the inverse healing length.

concepts.name: Free-particle energy
concepts.statement: ϵ_q = ℏ²q²/2m, the energy of a free particle of wavevector q.

concepts.name: Speed of sound in a condensate
concepts.statement: The sound-like part of the spectrum moves at s = √(n₀U₀/m).

concepts.name: Bragg probing of the spectrum
concepts.statement: Two lasers create a quasiparticle when their momentum and energy difference matches the spectrum, q = k₁ − k₂ and ω_q = ω₁ − ω₂, even at zero temperature.

concepts.name: Landau criterion for superfluidity
concepts.statement: An object can create an excitation only above a critical velocity, so objects moving slower than the speed of sound feel no drag: the repulsive condensate is a superfluid.

concepts.name: Stability of an attractive condensate
concepts.statement: With U₀ < 0 the long-wavelength frequencies are imaginary, but a trap of size a_t allows no wavevector below 1/a_t, so a condensate is stable up to N_max ∼ a_t/|a| atoms and collapses beyond.

concepts.name: Condensate and thermal cloud after expansion
concepts.statement: After expansion a condensate's size follows from the uncertainty principle, ∼ ℏτ/a_cm, while a thermal cloud is gaussian; fitting a bimodal distribution measures the condensed fraction.

concepts.name: First-order coherence of a condensate
concepts.statement: Two condensates with well-defined phases interfere like split laser light; thermal atoms are coherent only over about a de Broglie wavelength, while a condensate's long-range coherence spans the whole cloud.

concepts.name: Atom laser
concepts.statement: Outcoupling atoms by RF into an untrapped state gives the atomic equivalent of a laser beam; two RF frequencies outcouple from two places, and the visibility of their fringes measures the coherence between them.

concepts.name: Fringes of two expanding condensates
concepts.statement: Two condensates separated by ∆R_s expand and interfere with fringes spaced by ∆R ∼ ℏτ/∆R_s m.

concepts.name: Relative phase by measurement
concepts.statement: Two condensates of known atom numbers acquire a relative phase through spontaneous symmetry breaking in the measurement: detecting atoms without knowing their source projects the phase and leaves the numbers uncertain.

concepts.name: Double-well toy model
concepts.statement: N cold atoms in two wells joined by tunnelling at rate t, with ground state the symmetric |+⟩ and excited state |−⟩ higher by 2t.

concepts.name: Noninteracting ground state
concepts.statement: Without interactions all N atoms share |+⟩, a state with a well-defined phase between the wells that for large N is close to a coherent state: a classical Josephson device.

concepts.name: Strongly interacting ground state
concepts.statement: When U₀ ≫ t the atoms pile up evenly in the two wells in a highly non-classical Fock state, with no first-order interference and no Gross-Pitaevskii description.

concepts.name: Making non-classical matter
concepts.statement: Non-classical states of matter need interactions stronger than kinetic energy and low losses: tighter confinement, as in an optical lattice, lowers the tunnelling, and a Feshbach resonance raises the scattering length.

concepts.name: Optical lattice potential
concepts.statement: Counterpropagating red-detuned beams make standing waves of period λ/2 whose dipole force holds atoms at the intensity maxima; three of them make a simple cubic lattice, parameterized like the double well by tunnelling and on-site interaction.

concepts.name: Lattice site as an oscillator
concepts.statement: Near each minimum the lattice is harmonic with frequency ν_T; for depths V₀ ≫ E_R, the analogue of the Lamb-Dicke limit, atoms localize and wavefunctions on different sites barely overlap.

concepts.name: Recoil energy of the lattice
concepts.statement: E_R = ℏ²K_L²/2m, the energy scale against which a lattice's depth V₀ is measured.

concepts.name: Expansion in localized states
concepts.statement: The field operator is expanded over sites, ψ̂ = Σ b̂_i W(r − r_i), the Wannier functions approximated by each site's oscillator ground state; tunnelling hybridizes the levels into Bloch bands.

concepts.name: On-site interaction
concepts.statement: To leading order atoms interact only with those on the same site, with strength U₀ of about the interaction of two atoms in one oscillator ground state.

concepts.name: Hopping between sites
concepts.statement: Nearest-neighbour overlaps let atoms hop between sites at rate t, entering the Hamiltonian with a negative sign.

concepts.name: Bose-Hubbard model
concepts.statement: Site energies, hopping and on-site interaction together make the Hubbard model, realized by a Bose condensate in an optical lattice whose U and t are tuned by the scattering length and the lattice depth.

concepts.name: Superfluid in a weak lattice
concepts.statement: For t ≫ U₀ the hopping is diagonal in momentum, −2t Σ b̂_k†b̂_k cos ka, and every atom sits in k = 0: neighbouring sites are coherent, the phase is well defined and the number per site fluctuates.

concepts.name: Mott insulator
concepts.statement: For U₀ ≫ t at unit filling the ground state holds one atom per site, frozen in place, lowered by an exchange energy −2t²/U₀; the number per site is fixed, so the phase between sites is not.

concepts.name: Filling factor
concepts.statement: The filling factor ν is the number of atoms per lattice site; at commensurate, integer filling a Mott phase can form.

concepts.name: Quantum phase transition
concepts.statement: Changing t/U₀ moves the system between superfluid and Mott insulator even at T = 0, a phase transition driven by quantum rather than thermal fluctuations.

concepts.name: Mean-field estimate of the transition
concepts.statement: Comparing a product of coherent states with the Mott state predicts the transition near 4zt ∼ U₀; a variational state mixing 0, 1 and 2 atoms gives 5zt ∼ U₀, the mean-field value U₀/zt ≈ 5.8.

concepts.name: Excitation gap
concepts.statement: The superfluid has a Bogoliubov spectrum, while the Mott insulator's is gapped by ∆ϵ ∼ U₀ − t; the gap vanishes at the transition.

concepts.name: Wedding-cake structure
concepts.statement: In the harmonic trap of a real lattice the Mott phase forms shells of filling ν rising in steps toward the centre, with thin superfluid regions between them.

concepts.name: Observing the transition
concepts.statement: Released atoms of the superfluid interfere into the reciprocal lattice, while the Mott insulator, with no first-order coherence, shows no pattern; ramping U₀/t up and back recovers the superfluid.
